formula.explanation: Converts via SI base (m³/s): result = value × (factor_from / factor_to). Factors are units per m³/s: m³/s=1, m³/h=3600, L/min=60000, L/s=1000, GPM=15850.

content.introduction: Convert flow rate units instantly between m3/h, GPM (gallons per minute), L/min, CFM, m3/s, and more. This flow unit converter supports all common engineering flow units for liquids and gases. Enter a value, select from and to units, and get instant conversion for pipe sizing, pump selection, and process engineering calculations.

faq.q: What is the conversion from m³/h to GPM?
faq.a: 1 m³/h = 4.403 US GPM. 1 m³/h = 3.666 UK (imperial) GPM.

faq.q: How do I convert mass flow to volumetric flow?
faq.a: Volumetric flow (m³/s) = mass flow (kg/s) / density (kg/m³). For water, 1 kg/s ≈ 3.6 m³/h.

faq.q: How do you convert m3/h to GPM?
faq.a: 1 m3/h = 4.403 US GPM. To convert m3/h to GPM, multiply by 4.403. For example, 10 m3/h = 44.03 GPM. Use this converter for instant results with any flow unit.

faq.q: How do you convert L/min to m3/h?
faq.a: 1 L/min = 0.06 m3/h. To convert L/min to m3/h, multiply by 0.06. For example, 100 L/min = 6 m3/h.

faq.q: What is CFM and how do you convert it?
faq.a: CFM (Cubic Feet per Minute) is a flow unit for gases. 1 CFM = 1.699 m3/h = 0.472 L/s. CFM is commonly used for HVAC and compressed air systems.

faq.q: What flow units does this converter support?
faq.a: This converter supports: m3/h, m3/s, L/min, L/s, GPM (US), GPM (UK), CFM, and mm3/s. All conversions are based on standard SI unit relationships.
